If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-2}{{x}^{2}-9} & =\frac{\sqrt{3+1}-2}{{3}^{2}-9}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-2}{{x}^{2}-9} & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-2}{(x-3)(x+3)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{(\sqrt{x+1}-2)(\sqrt{x+1}+2)}{(x-3)(x+3)(\sqrt{x+1}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{{(\sqrt{x+1})}^{2}-{2}^{2}}{(x-3)(x+3)(\sqrt{x+1}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{x+1-4}{(x-3)(x+3)(\sqrt{x+1}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{x-3}{(x-3)(x+3)(\sqrt{x+1}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{1}{(x+3)(\sqrt{x+1}+2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(3+3)(\sqrt{3+1}+2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$
